chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyab, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:
Indeed, from backbiting is that you say about your brother that which Allah has concealed upon him, and indeed, slander is that you say about your brother that which is not in him.

key_terms.أَخِيكَ: Your brother; referring to a fellow Muslim or person of faith.
key_terms.الْبَهْتَانَ: Slander; attributing to a person a quality or action that they do not possess.
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: Backbiting; mentioning a person in their absence regarding a fault they possess.
key_terms.سَتَرَهُ اللَّهُ: Allah concealed; referring to faults or sins that are not publicly known.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between backbiting and slander in Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a precise jurisprudential distinction between *ghaybah* (backbiting), which involves revealing existing but concealed faults, and *bahitan* (slander), which involves attributing non-existent faults. This clarification is foundational in Shia ethics for evaluating the severity of verbal sins, as backbiting is often considered more common and subtle, while slander is a deliberate fabrication. The narration underscores the social responsibility of Muslims to protect the honor of their brethren, reflecting the broader Quranic emphasis on preserving communal dignity.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman bin Sayaba, from al-Sadiq, Ja’far bin Muhammed, peace be upon them both, that he said:
Indeed, it is from backbiting that you say about your brother that which Allah has concealed upon him, and indeed, it is from slander that you say about your brother that which is not in him.
